quote.text: When the facts change, I change my mind — what do you do, sir?
quote.author: widely attributed to John Maynard Keynes; the exact wording is disputed

stories.headline: The Panopticon, Now a Suite
stories.dek: Hoshino Resorts has opened its ninth HOSHINOYA flagship inside a decommissioned Meiji prison in Nara — the last intact survivor of the great 1900s jails. The solitary cells have been knocked together into forty-eight red-brick rooms. It is the most literal revision in the book: a place built to confine, reopened to indulge.

stories.headline: The Men Who Build the Whole Car in a Spare Room
stories.dek: Most people who play a racing game use a controller. A devoted world bolts a motor-driven wheel to an aluminium frame, spends more on the brake pedal than the game, and slowly turns a spare room into a cockpit. This week the industry that sells them the parts consolidated under one roof — and a challenger torched the price of torque.

stories.headline: A Corridor on Paper, and Not One Ship Through It
stories.dek: A week on, Iran and Oman say their Hormuz route is in "final drafting." Nothing has been signed, no hull has run it, and the fee it hangs on is still called a toll by one side and a service charge by the other. The announcement has outrun the fact.

stories.headline: The Parade Is Tomorrow; the Policy Is a Fortnight Away
stories.dek: The country's sixty-first birthday brings the parade back indoors on Sunday, an aerial drone display under the shut roof, and a leader's eve-of-holiday address tonight. What actually reaches a family's budget arrives a fortnight on, at the Rally on the 23rd.

stories.headline: One Bid for the Land — and It Set the Record
stories.dek: A state land tender in Telok Blangah drew a single offer, well short of the four-to-six developers analysts expected. Then read the price: it cleared above the top of the guide and set a new benchmark rate for a city-fringe residential plot. The turnout said caution; the number said conviction.

stories.headline: The First Open Max-Class Weights Are a Week Away — Again
stories.dek: Alibaba shipped its biggest model, Qwen3.8-Max, as a closed API this week, and promised to open the weights "next week." If it does, it would be the first time a frontier Max-tier model goes downloadable. As of today it hasn't, and there is no licence line yet. Promised is not shipped.

stories.kicker: The Kit · One Body, Every Angle
stories.headline: Insta360 Puts a One-Inch Sensor in a Camera That Films Everything
stories.dek: The X6, teased this week for a 12 August launch, is the biggest leap the 360 line has taken in years: dual one-inch sensors, a triple AI chip, 8K capture. Point it, film the whole sphere, and choose the shot afterwards. The catch, as ever with a teaser, is that not one reviewer has held it.

stories.headline: Phoebe Bridgers Arrives on a Wall of Perfect Scores
stories.dek: Lost Weekend lands on 14 August under near-universal critical acclaim — a Metacritic in the low nineties, a scattering of perfect tens six days early. The revision to watch is the one the users are already making: the boards are cooler than the broadsheets, and that gap will outlast the release-day scores.

stories.headline: The Study That Undercuts the Ban
stories.dek: A prospective analysis of the largest child-brain cohort finds the lever on a child's screen use was never the rule you set — it was the habit you modelled. What parents do with their own phones predicts what their children do with theirs, more reliably than any limit imposed from above. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: America Lost Jobs in July — and the Whole Regime Flipped
stories.dek: Payrolls didn't just miss; they went negative, the first contraction since February, with 103,000 shaved off the prior two months. In an afternoon the hawkish "maybe a hike" story became a "when's the cut" story. Gold set a record, the dollar fell, and equities made new highs on the worst possible reason.

stories.headline: The Number on Your Watch May Forecast Your Brain
stories.dek: A nine-year follow-up to a landmark Norwegian trial finds that a single measure of fitness — VO2 max, the one your wearable already estimates — predicts brain volume and memory a decade on, more reliably than which exercise programme people were assigned. The twist is who aged best. Not medical advice.

stories.headline: What Changed at the Airport
stories.dek: Two entry-rule clocks moved this fortnight, a First-Class cabin came back on a European route, and the friction that will actually annoy a camera-buying reader is the end of Japan's walk-out tax-free shopping. The delta, read first through Changi.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking
stories.dek: One thing to act on before lunch: seats for a Tokyo sumo tournament open this morning, and the good ones empty out by dusk. Beyond it, a packed Singapore autumn fronted by the Grand Prix's debut Sprint weekend.

stories.headline: The Country With Two Seasons
stories.dek: In December, Japan gave a name to a loss it had felt for a decade: niki — "two seasons." A meteorologist's observation became a national buzzword. The story isn't the weather. It's the first time a rich country has watched climate change come not for its coastline, but for its self-image — and reached for a word to mourn it.
